text:
Gabe Perreault has spent the season on the Rangers' top line with Mika Zibanejad and Alexis Lafrenière, and at 21 he's holding his own. He has six goals and nine points in 18 games, the Rangers take about 55% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and his finishing is right where his chances say it should be.

The 23rd pick in 2023 out of Boston College is running well ahead of forwards drafted around him. The median first full season for picks 18 to 28 is 0.37 points a game; he's at 0.50. His last ten games have been all goals, three of them and no assists, which is the kind of quirk that evens out.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (eight games, so treat it loosely) shows 60% of his shots come off the rush, and NHL Edge has his top speed in the top quarter of the league. That's a winger built for the transition game Mike Sullivan wants. Our range projects 17 to 30 goals over a full season, and nothing about his start looks like luck doing the work.
headline: Perreault belongs on the top line
